unlisted_practices: Implement robust privacy safeguards to protect patient information and ensure ethical data collection and AI usage.
Design AI tools to ensure fair access for all individuals regardless of socioeconomic status.
Establish policies to prevent insurers from misusing AI-generated health risk assessments to adjust premiums or penalize individuals.
Strengthen partnerships across academia, government, and industry to enhance data sharing and interoperability, particularly through wearable technologies, while safeguarding privacy.
Foster cross-disciplinary initiatives such as citizen science to collect real-world evidence and promote community engagement.
Leverage large biobank programs such as All of Us for diabetes precision health AI.
Encourage federal agencies to take a proactive role in supporting infrastructure development, education, and coordination of community efforts for AI in diabetes precision health.

screen.reason: This article summarizes an NIH workshop on AI in Diabetes Precision Health, outlining recommendations, opportunities, and strategic challenges rather than presenting empirical data.
